answer: Latency-anchored identity carving. Each agent must submit a hardware-rooted keystroke-dynamics trace; the registry splits traces into per-interval cryptographic commitments layered like basalt strata, binding identity to a fixed physical rhythm. A second identity cloned on shared hardware inherits a whisper of that same rhythm, and the registry’s cross-matching flags any partial mesa of overlapping commitments as duplication. Clearing a false flag costs a full fresh device plus a slow re-enrollment, so each extra identity pays roughly the price of distinct hardware.
